objective: Make only the cruush landing page discoverable to search engines and answer engines, while keeping every member surface out of every index, and give non-JavaScript crawlers something to read. Add static About, Help and Blog pages outside the application so they are readable without JavaScript.
userOutcome: A search for cruush, and a question put to an answer engine, can resolve to cruush.app with an accurate description, without any member profile, photo or message becoming reachable or indexable.
audience: Search and answer-engine crawlers, and people who find cruush through them.
successCriteria: Every member route returns the noindex header, including after the SPA fallback rewrite.
robots.txt allows the landing page, disallows member routes, and names the answer-engine crawlers explicitly.
A crawler that does not run JavaScript reads a real description of cruush at /.
The JSON-LD block survives the Vite build byte-identical, so its Content-Security-Policy hash still matches.
The frontend still builds and every member route still serves the application.
/about, /help and /blog return 200 with index, follow, and serve real HTML without JavaScript.
Each page's JSON-LD survives the build and its sha256 is present in the Content-Security-Policy.
Every body block a human must write is visibly marked as needing copy.
About, Help and Blog appear in the shared policy link list, so they render both in Settings and at the bottom of the signed-out landing screen.
The static pages resolve at the same URLs in vite dev and preview as they do behind nginx.
mustPreserve: Every existing security header, including the Content-Security-Policy, which must not gain unsafe-inline.
The existing visual design and copy authored by Julien. No new page, route or visible UI.
The SPA fallback: every member route continues to serve the application.
That no member data is reachable without authentication.
nonGoals: Designing UI. Julien is the only designer.
Any PostHog, analytics or Google Analytics change.
Deploying. This is a local branch only.
Writing the body copy for the new pages. Julien supplies it; the pages ship with marked placeholders and no invented product claims.
Changing how the policy link list is laid out or styled. Only its entries change.

assumptions.statement: The landing page is the logged-out Auth screen, since App.tsx renders Auth for every path without a session, and it contains no member data.
assumptions.impact: If a logged-out route ever server-renders member content, indexing / would expose it. Nothing renders server side today.

assumptions.statement: The wording of the description sentence is a placeholder pending Julien's decision; only the mechanism is being delivered.
assumptions.impact: The sentence appears in the meta description, the JSON-LD, llms.txt and the noscript block. Changing it means changing those four places together.

assumptions.statement: The new pages are plain static documents rather than React routes, because answer-engine crawlers do not execute JavaScript.
assumptions.impact: They do not share the application's design system, so they will look simpler than the product until someone decides otherwise.

nextVisibleMilestone: cruush.app can be indexed and cited with an accurate description while every member surface stays invisible.
stopConditions: Any member route would become indexable.
A change would require new UI or new copy beyond the description sentence.
requiredEvidence: nginx -t passes against the real config in an nginx:1.27-alpine container.
Serving the real built dist, / returns index, follow and /map, /messages and /profile/:id return noindex.
The noscript description is present in the raw HTML of the built /.
The sha256 of the JSON-LD in the built dist/index.html equals the hash in the Content-Security-Policy.
vite build exits 0 and robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt are emitted to dist.
Serving the real built dist, /about, /about/, /help and /blog return 200 with index, follow, while /map, /messages and an unknown path return noindex.
The extracted text of /about contains the page content with no JavaScript executed.
